note.label: 2 Samuel 9: David Shows Kindness for Jonathan's Sake

precepts.why:
David asked, “Is there yet any that is left of the house of Saul, that I may shew him kindness for Jonathan’s sake?” Saul's son Jonathan and David were always very close.

That closeness goes back to the beef between Saul and David in the book of Samuel. Jonathan was always there for David; that was David's homeboy. “Then Jonathan and David made a covenant, because he loved him as his own soul.”

So even with Saul gone, David remembered the covenant, and sought out whoever was left of Saul's house to show him kindness for Jonathan's sake.

points: David asked whether there was yet any left of the house of Saul that he might show him kindness for Jonathan's sake. Remember that Saul's son Jonathan and David were always very close.
That closeness goes back to the beef between Saul and David in the book of Samuel; Jonathan was always there for David, that was David's homeboy, they were really close.

note.label: 2 Samuel 9: David Shows Kindness for Jonathan's Sake

points: A servant of the house of Saul named Ziba was brought to David. When David asked whether there was yet any of the house of Saul that he might show the kindness of God unto him, Ziba said Jonathan had yet a son who was lame on his feet, dwelling in the house of Machir the son of Ammiel in Lodebar.

note.label: 2 Samuel 9: David Shows Kindness for Jonathan's Sake

points: The king sent and fetched him out of Lodebar. Because of the respect and love David had for Jonathan, David was going to show kindness to Jonathan's son, even though the son could not walk.

note.label: 2 Samuel 9: David Shows Kindness for Jonathan's Sake

points: To show his love for Jonathan, David gave everything that Saul owned to Jonathan's son.

note.label: 2 Samuel 9: David Shows Kindness for Jonathan's Sake

points: When Mephibosheth the son of Jonathan came unto David he fell on his face and did reverence. David told him, Fear not, for I will surely show thee kindness for Jonathan thy father's sake, and will restore thee all the land of Saul thy father, and thou shalt eat bread at my table continually.

note.label: 2 Samuel 9: David Shows Kindness for Jonathan's Sake

points: Mephibosheth bowed himself and asked what David saw in such a dead dog as he was. David then called Ziba and gave unto his master's son all that pertained to Saul, and charged Ziba, his sons, and his servants to till the land and bring in the fruits, that Mephibosheth might have food, though he himself would eat at the king's table always.

Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants. This shows the level of riches Israel had as a nation: Saul's servant had servants of his own, that is how wealthy this man was, and all of them were set to till the land and take care of the house for Mephibosheth, all out of the respect David had for Jonathan.

note.label: 2 Samuel 9: David Shows Kindness for Jonathan's Sake

points: Mephibosheth had a young son named Micha, and all that dwelt in the house of Ziba were servants unto Mephibosheth, who dwelt in Jerusalem and did eat continually at the king's table, and was lame on both his feet.
